content:
Apple has confirmed that it will hold a special product launch event called "Welcome Home" next Tuesday (October 13), but it has not yet announced whether a keynote video will be released simultaneously on the day. Here is what we know so far.

Apple has not confirmed a "Welcome Home" keynote, but Mark Gurman says there will be an "online video presentation."

Apple has been revamping its traditional product launch approach throughout this year. The MacBook Neo released in March was the first example — after announcing multiple new products via press releases over several consecutive days, it was unveiled through an "in-person experience" event where media could try out the devices hands-on.

It looks like Apple's "Welcome Home" event on October 13 will also break new ground in a similar fashion.

Unlike previous events, Apple has not yet added "Welcome Home" to its Apple Events webpage. There are no signs of any livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app either.

Things could change in the days leading up to the event, but based on the current situation, it appears that there will not be a keynote video on October 13.

However, Mark Gurman mentioned a video presentation in a Bloomberg report. Writing in an article discussing another Apple event scheduled for October 27, Gurman stated:

According to Gurman — who has previously accurately reported the October 13 date as well as the fact that the event will focus on home products — Apple will hold an "online video presentation" next week.

Media will attend the "Apple Experience" hands-on event starting at 9 a.m. local time in New York on the day. So if a launch video is released that day, it will most likely go live around that time, which is considerably earlier than the typical keynote broadcast time.

We expect at least three new products to be unveiled on Tuesday, and you can find the details here.

What do you think — will Apple release a keynote video for "Welcome Home"? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
